nv_left_south_wall.blurb: This is the first wall you meet when walking into The Gun Club, a small limestone canyon on the western fringe of Las Vegas. It holds 27 routes, nearly all bolted sport lines plus a single top-rope. Grades start in the 5.4 to 5.8 range but the wall leans toward the harder end, with plenty of 5.10s and a good run of 5.11 and 5.12 lines. The face looks north, so it stays cool from mid-morning and only catches a short burst of late sun, which makes it a good pick when the rest of the valley is baking. Expect sharp, technical limestone that is tough on fingertips.

nv_sunnyside_crags.blurb: A trad-only cliff on the north side of Icebox Canyon in Red Rock, close to the road and reached by a short canyon hike. Its 26 routes are on sandstone and run from 5.7 up to the low 5.12s, with most of the weight between 5.9 and 5.11. Because of how the canyon is oriented, the wall is sunny through summer and shady in winter, so the comfortable window is narrower than at many neighbouring crags. It is easy to hike past, so watch for the corner features on the right wall. Wet sandstone breaks easily, so wait for it to dry fully after rain.

nv_story_crag_main_wall.blurb: The largest wall at the Old Spanish Trail crags, high on the west flank of Mt Potosi at roughly 6,500 feet. All 26 routes are bolted sport lines on limestone, long enough that a 70 m rope and a generous set of draws are worthwhile. It suits stronger climbers: most routes sit around 5.11, with several 5.12s, a handful of 5.10s and one lone 5.8. The face looks north-northwest and sees only a few hours of sun in high summer, so it stays cold much of the year and can hold snow into June, but it is a relief when the city is hot. Helmets are wise because some loose rock remains.
nv_story_crag_main_wall.approach: A steep climb with about 800 feet of gain in under a mile. Head east from where you leave the car, cross the wash, and pick up a faint trail; allow roughly half an hour or more depending on your pack.

nv_flight_path_area.blurb: A set of short, east-facing sandstone walls on the lower slopes of Bridge Mountain in Pine Creek Canyon, Red Rock. The 26 routes are all trad, mostly one pitch, and moderate: grades run from 5.6 to 5.10 with the bulk between 5.7 and 5.9. Several lines share anchors in clusters, so a party can lead an easy one and then top-rope something harder beside it. Sun arrives in the morning only, leaving the walls shaded by afternoon. Higher ledges and a small tower have more varied climbs, some with doubtful rock low down. The sandstone is delicate when damp, so do not climb on it after rain.

nv_stratocaster_area.blurb: Spread over several walls at the west end of the Calico Hills in Red Rock, this is a sunny sandstone area with 25 routes, most of them bolted sport lines and a few trad. It is a place for hard climbing: nothing is easy, with a few 5.10s, a big cluster of 5.11 and 5.12 routes and a small number at 5.13. The rock varies from slabby to steep and from thin edges to juggy holds. Facing southwest, it bakes through the afternoon, which makes it a winter favourite; in warm months climbers get on early. Parking at the second pullout fills quickly, so arrive early or use the neighbouring pullout.
